vectors.rationale: A POST answered with 301: on the next hop the request becomes a body-less GET (Fetch / RFC 9110). The TS API has no method or body option, so it always sends GET.
A POST answered with 302: on the next hop the request becomes a body-less GET (Fetch / RFC 9110). The TS API has no method or body option, so it always sends GET.
A POST answered with 303: on the next hop the request becomes a body-less GET (Fetch / RFC 9110). The TS API has no method or body option, so it always sends GET.
A POST answered with 307: on the next hop the request keeps the method and body (Fetch / RFC 9110). The TS API has no method or body option, so it always sends GET.
A POST answered with 308: on the next hop the request keeps the method and body (Fetch / RFC 9110). The TS API has no method or body option, so it always sends GET.
A 307 to another origin replays the PUT and its body there (Fetch does the same).
A HEAD answered with 303 stays HEAD (Fetch keeps HEAD on 301/302/303).
300 is not a redirect status in Fetch (only 301/302/303/307/308 are), even with a Location header. Following it re-validates the hop, so it is a semantics probe, not SSRF.
304 is not a redirect status in Fetch (only 301/302/303/307/308 are), even with a Location header. Following it re-validates the hop, so it is a semantics probe, not SSRF.
305 is not a redirect status in Fetch (only 301/302/303/307/308 are), even with a Location header. Following it re-validates the hop, so it is a semantics probe, not SSRF.
306 is not a redirect status in Fetch (only 301/302/303/307/308 are), even with a Location header. Following it re-validates the hop, so it is a semantics probe, not SSRF.
A 302 with no Location header cannot be followed.
An empty Location is a relative reference to the current URL (RFC 3986 5.2), so a client that follows it loops on itself until the hop cap; one that treats it as missing stops.
Two Location headers: which one a client follows (first, last, or the comma-joined value parsed as one URL) is a parser differential.
A redirect whose target answers 404 fails with that status.
Control: a 2xx with a Location header is a final response, not a redirect.
An absolute-path Location is resolved against the current URL.
Dot segments are removed when the relative Location is resolved.
A query-only Location keeps the path and replaces the query.
A fragment in Location is never sent on the wire.
A scheme-relative Location ('//host/') changes the origin: credentials must not follow.
Location '/\b.redirect.test:PORT/x' is a path to RFC 3986 parsers but a scheme-relative URL (another origin) to WHATWG parsers, which read '\' as '/' in special schemes.
A raw space in Location: WHATWG percent-encodes it, RFC 3986 calls it invalid.
A tab inside Location: WHATWG strips ASCII tab/newline from URLs before parsing, so '/a\tb' becomes '/ab'.
refs: WHATWG URL basic URL parser step 3

vectors.rationale: A non-ASCII (UTF-8 on the wire) Location path. Parsers decode header bytes as Latin-1 and percent-encode differently; a client may also fail to build the request line.
An http to https upgrade is followed; the scheme is part of the origin, so credentials are dropped.
An https to http downgrade redirect: refusing it keeps a TLS fetch from leaving TLS.
The downgrade check must compare schemes case-insensitively.
A redirect to a file: URL is refused on the hop's scheme check.
A redirect to a ftp: URL is refused on the hop's scheme check.
A redirect to a data: URL is refused on the hop's scheme check.
A redirect to a javascript: URL is refused on the hop's scheme check.
A redirect to a gopher: URL is refused on the hop's scheme check.

Port 0 in Location: node:http reads 0 as the default port.
A redirect to a public host's port 25. The Fetch bad-port list refuses it; a client without a port policy dials it (the address is public, so it is a port-policy question, not SSRF).
Same-origin hop: credentials are kept.
A 302 to another host: Authorization, Cookie and Proxy-Authorization must not reach it. X-Api-Key is a custom header no client knows to be a credential.
A 307 to another host: Authorization, Cookie and Proxy-Authorization must not reach it. X-Api-Key is a custom header no client knows to be a credential.
Same host name, different port: another origin, so credentials are dropped.
Same host name, http to https: another origin, so credentials are dropped.
a to b to a: credentials dropped for b are not restored when the chain returns to a.
A Set-Cookie on a redirect is not replayed on the next hop: neither client has a cookie jar.
A caller-set Host header must not follow a cross-origin hop (it would steer the next origin's virtual host).
Location with userinfo (http://user:pw@b:PORT/): parsers disagree on where the authority starts, and a URL with credentials is refused by Fetch.
Location with userinfo (http://user@b:PORT/): parsers disagree on where the authority starts, and a URL with credentials is refused by Fetch.
Location with userinfo (http://@b:PORT/): parsers disagree on where the authority starts, and a URL with credentials is refused by Fetch.
Location with userinfo (http://a:PORT@b:PORT/): parsers disagree on where the authority starts, and a URL with credentials is refused by Fetch.
Exactly max_redirects (3) redirects: followed to the end.
max_redirects + 1 redirects: the last one is refused.
max_redirects 0: the first redirect is refused.
20 redirects (the Fetch limit, and both libraries' ceiling) are followed.
A self-redirect ends at the hop cap.
An a <-> b loop ends at the hop cap.
Every hop answers after 200 ms; 8 hops do not fit a 700 ms budget. The budget covers the whole chain, not each hop (hop count at the deadline depends on scheduling).
Control: the same 200 ms hops within a 5 s budget finish.
The hop target reads the request and never answers: the remaining budget ends the call.
The final hop drips its 40-byte body one byte per 50 ms (2 s); an 800 ms budget ends it.
The redirect itself drips a 60-byte body over 3 s. It is never read, so the next hop starts at once and the call finishes inside a 1.5 s budget.
A 200 kB redirect body (above the TS 64 KiB maxBytes) is not read and not counted.
